Routing observations:
- Option C was rejected for 9 of 10 tickets, with the system explicitly stating “option C is not valid.”
- The sole successful C selection was REQ-2408: a small shipment from the north region, submitted by Regional Ops after a bounced first attempt. Its C label appeared as “regional…”/“regional office.”
- Do not select C by default; it may only be valid for a narrow regional-office case, possibly north-region shipments handled by Regional Ops.
- No evidence yet distinguishes when to choose A (standard queue) versus B (priority desk). Ticket size, request type, region, sender, and urgency wording may affect this, but the failed examples cannot establish the rule because C was selected every time.
- For future tickets, inspect the complete option labels and prefer A or B unless the request clearly matches the validated regional-office pattern.

Routing observations:
- Prior baseline: C was rejected on 9/10 attempts; sole success was REQ-2408, a small north-region shipment from Regional Ops after a bounced first attempt. C displayed as “regional office.” Treat this as a narrow, unconfirmed pattern—not a default.
- New success: REQ-2410 accepted A for a small east-region claim from Regional Ops. Thus A can be valid for at least some Regional Ops/small requests; the rule is not simply “regional office → C.”
- Rejections:
  - A invalid for a large north invoice (Field Sales), large north shipment (Finance Desk), large south shipment (Finance Desk), small east shipment (Client Services), small south claim (Regional Ops), and small south shipment (Regional Ops).
  - B invalid for large east claim (Finance Desk and Field Sales) and large east invoice (Field Sales).
- No new C or D selections were tested. Some option lists now visibly include D; inspect the complete labels before choosing.
- Ticket size, request type, region, sender/desk, urgency, and wording may jointly determine the route. “Regional office” wording alone is not validated: east-region large claims explicitly mentioning it still had B rejected, but C was not tried.
- Procedure-change memos mention upcoming refund/shipment changes; do not assume they alter current routing unless the ticket or options specify this.
- For future tickets, use elimination from known outcomes, read all option labels, and avoid repeating rejected choices. Prefer neither A nor B by default; consider C/D when their full labels and ticket attributes provide a clear match.

Routing observations:
- Outcomes are highly attribute-dependent; no simple region/size/request rule is established. Consider request type, region, size, sender/desk, urgency, wording, and exact option labels together.
- Prior success: A for REQ-2410, a small east claim from Regional Ops.
- C successes remain limited to REQ-2408 (small north shipment, Regional Ops, after a bounced first attempt). New C rejections: small north claim (Regional Ops), small east refund (Regional Ops), small east invoice (Regional Ops), and small east shipment (Regional Ops). Do not default “Regional Ops” or “regional office” to C.
- D successes: REQ-2423 (small east invoice, Partner Accounts) and REQ-2429 (large north claim, Partner Accounts). D rejections: large south claim from Field Sales, large north refund from Field Sales, and large south claim from Partner Accounts. D may fit some Partner Accounts requests but is not universally valid.
- B rejections include large north shipment (Finance Desk), large east claims (Finance Desk and Field Sales), and large east invoice (Field Sales). A rejections include multiple large north/south requests plus small east shipment and small south claim/shipment; avoid repeating A where applicable.
- Recent wording such as “scanned, not typed,” “second attempt,” and urgency has not yielded a reliable standalone rule.
- Procedure-change memos concern upcoming invoice/claim/refund/shipment changes; do not apply them unless the ticket or options explicitly indicate they are active.
- Always inspect the complete option labels (including D), use known rejections to eliminate choices, and treat every accepted route as narrow evidence rather than a general rule.

Routing observations:
- Outcomes are highly attribute-dependent; no simple region/size/request rule is established. Consider request type, region, size, sender/desk, urgency, wording, and exact option labels together.
- A successes: REQ-2410 (small east claim, Regional Ops) and REQ-2436 (small north refund, Partner Accounts). A has many rejections, including large north/south requests, small east shipment, small south claim/shipment, small north invoice (Client Services), and large east invoice (Field Sales). Do not default to A.
- B success: REQ-2431 (small east shipment, Partner Accounts). B rejections include large north shipment (Finance Desk), large east claims (Finance Desk and Field Sales), large east invoice (Field Sales), and small south claims/invoices from Regional Ops. Do not infer that urgency or “same as last month” favors B.
- C success remains limited to REQ-2408 (small north shipment, Regional Ops, after a bounced first attempt). C rejections now include small north claim, small east refund/invoice/shipment (Regional Ops), large south invoice (Finance Desk), and other Regional Ops cases. Do not default regional-office wording or Regional Ops to C.
- D successes: REQ-2423 (small east invoice, Partner Accounts), REQ-2429 (large north claim, Partner Accounts), and REQ-2432 (large north claim, Finance Desk). D rejections include large north invoice (Field Sales), large south claim (Field Sales and Partner Accounts), and others; it is not universal.
- Recent wording (“scanned, not typed,” “second attempt,” urgency, “no rush,” etc.) has no reliable standalone rule. Scanned wording appears across both accepted and rejected routes.
- Procedure-change memos concern upcoming shipment/invoice changes; do not apply them unless the ticket/options explicitly indicate they are active.
- Inspect complete option labels, including D; use known rejections to eliminate choices, and treat accepted routes as narrow evidence.
